edit.description: Add FlumeApi.paths: {repoRoot, configDir, flumeDir}; buildFlumeApi(paths) takes them as a required argument instead of zero args. All three stay required — that requirement IS the mechanism the per section names.

loadChainModule and diskChainLoader gain the roots and pass them to buildFlumeApi at the single factory-application seam (~:1064, `factory(buildFlumeApi())`). Also the supervisor's own diskChainLoader call (~:4574).

Five diskChainLoader sites (~:126 chainRefusesPhase, :345 status, :478 check, :566 friction, :652 resolveChain), all in main() scope which already holds repoRoot (~:135) and flumeDir/configDir from resolveStateDirs (~:240). Pass flumeDir into runJobVerb (~:253) and repoRoot into jobRun (~:275).
runJobVerb(args, repoRoot, configDir) gains a fourth flumeDir param, used by `job status`'s diskChainLoader (~:42) and passed into JobNewOptions (~:116).
JobNewOptions gains flumeDir, JobRunOptions gains repoRoot; thread both into the two loadChainModule calls (~:176 jobNew, ~:279 jobRun).

chainLoadGate (~:260) reads ctx.repoRoot/configDir/flumeDir, all already on GateContext. Declare at the site that under afterCommit repoRoot is the ephemeral worktree while flumeDir is the primary checkout's state root (spec/chain.md, What a gate receives) — correct here since the gate validates a chain rather than running a tick, but it should read deliberate.
A chain factory sees api.paths matching the Dispatcher's own resolved roots.

summary: FlumeApi carries paths {repoRoot, configDir, flumeDir}, the dispatcher's own resolved roots, by reference
tests: api.paths.flumeDir/configDir/repoRoot equal the Dispatcher's own resolved values at chain-load time
acceptance: a chain can resolve a per-run artifact against api.paths.flumeDir instead of process.env.FLUME_DIR with a `?? CHAIN_DIR` fallback
notes: Fence widened by plan 2026-09-06 after four build parks: the change needs all nine call sites and only plan can declare them. Optional roots are NOT an option — attempt 1 (36907e3) defaulted them and handed chainLoadGate a repoRoot of .flume/ (engineering.md, Loud or nothing). tests/chain.test.ts and tests/examples.integration.test.ts also call buildFlumeApi() bare; they ride build's tests/** channel.

edit.description: The gate-revert record's details digest (~:4158) uses tailBound, keeping the last 8KB. For a suite reporter the tail is the pass list and the count line; the failure block sits in the elided head. Keep the failure lines first, then fill remaining budget. tailBound's own JSDoc justifies the tail for an agent's final message (~:4945, voluntary-bail) — that reasoning is right there and wrong here, so the two sites want different helpers, not a shared one re-pointed.
Drive a gate whose details exceed MAX_PRIOR_DETAILS with the failure block at the head.

summary: The gate-revert prior-attempt digest keeps the failure block, not the trailing pass list — a retry agent reads why it was reverted

per.section: Prior-outcome feedback to the retrying tick

tests: a gate-revert record whose gate details exceed the cap retains the failing-test lines and marks the elision
acceptance: a reverted build tick's <prior-attempt> block names which tests failed, not only how many
notes: Field-traced: four records on 2026-09-06 carried a count and no name, and .flume/prior-attempts/flumeapi-paths.json opens with `[truncated 16751 chars]…` with the failure detail inside the elision — the attempt-1 retry agent diagnosed from that gap and recorded a cause that was later disproved. The per section already demands the digest carry the gate's details; keeping the wrong slice is the defect.
